The measured terminology rules (voice-terminology.md) come first; the word-level rules from the other harness files (small rules, banned vocabulary, words and usage) follow.

# Terminology profile

Word choice, descriptive language, emphasis, naming. All rules are `[advisory]` and descriptive: they record what the 26 published posts do, never quotas. Evidence: `analysis/terminology_freq.md`, regenerated by `python3 -I analysis/terminology_freq.py` (26 posts, about 26,600 words after stripping code, URLs and images). A rule is here only when 3+ posts support it. Post slugs are shortened to their distinctive start. Approved by Ricardo on 2026-10-22.

### Word choice

**Plain, spoken verbs for work: use, build, want, need, start, create.** Favor ordinary active verbs over abstract ones. Pooled rate per 1k words: use 2.4, using 2.25, want 1.95, building 1.9, build 1.9, need 1.3. `build`/`building` appear in 21 and 18 of 26 posts, `use`/`using` in 18 and 23. Posts with no `leverage`-class verb are the norm (see `G-05`).
- "I built this dashboard using: Python 3.10, Beautiful Soup..." (`building-your-own-football-analytics`)
- "I wanted to identify two players profiles" (`how-to-scrape-transfermarkt`)
- Supports: `building-your-own-football-analytics`, `how-to-scrape-transfermarkt`, `embrace-your-weirdness`, `shipping-a-rag-system`, `how-to-use-tool-calling`, `a-claude-skill-to-build`.

**"I want to / I wanted to" states the purpose before the how.** 35 hits in 17 posts.
- "I want to show you how it works." (`building-a-rag-system`)
- Supports: `how-to-use-fbref`, `how-to-scrape-transfermarkt`, `building-a-rag-system`, `a-claude-skill-to-build`.

**Name the domain concretely: data, football, metrics, team, match, pipeline.** `data` is the top content word (9.4 per 1k, 24 of 26 posts); `football` is in 22 posts. Recurring phrases: "football analytics" (13 posts), "data sources" (9), "match reports" (6), "event data" (5), "RAG system" (5), "vector database" (4).
- "building AI systems, using football analytics as the sandbox" (`embrace-your-weirdness`)
- Supports: `building-a-rag-system`, `rag-is-a-data-engineering`, `from-vibes-to-metrics`, `how-to-use-fbref`, `the-art-of-football-data-scouting`.

**Football, never soccer.** "football" 98 hits in 22 posts; "soccer" 2 hits, both inside titles of other people's links (`5-actionable-tips`, `how-to-use-fbref`).

**"System" and "pipeline" for what he builds, not "solution" or "platform".** "system" 77 hits in 13 posts, "pipeline" 18 in 8, "tool/tools" 53 in 14.
- "Building a RAG System That Generates Football Post-Match Tactical Reports" (title, `building-a-rag-system`)
- Supports: `rag-is-a-data-engineering`, `shipping-a-rag-system`, `how-to-scrape-transfermarkt`, `understanding-model-context-protocol`.

**Loose connectors and contractions.** Contractions in all 26 posts (I'm/I've/I'll/I'd in 21). Sentences open with But/And/So in 12 posts, "Here's" in 10.
- "But fortunately there's a tool that can solve all of these problems" (`uv-the-tool`)
- Supports: `uv-the-tool`, `from-vibes-to-metrics`, `a-thank-you-two-ideas`, `using-agentic-ides`.

### Descriptive language

**Practical, concrete adjectives: specific, free, key, real, simple, best.** Each appears in 15+ posts (specific 17, free 20, key 15, real 15, best 17). They qualify scope or cost, rarely feeling.
- "real data from top providers like StatsBomb, Tracab, Opta" (`embrace-your-weirdness`)
- "Free Tier: It provided the perfect 'sandbox' for the MVP" (`shipping-a-rag-system`)
- Supports: `building-your-own-football-analytics`, `how-to-use-fbref`, `uv-the-tool`, `embrace-your-weirdness`.

**"Free" is a recurring selling point.** 41 hits in 20 posts, partly from the Subscribe footer; outside the footer: "free data", "free tier", "free sources".
- "Building Your Own Football Analytics Dashboards With Free Data" (`building-your-own-football-analytics`)
- Supports: `how-to-use-fbref`, `5-actionable-tips`, `building-a-rag-system`, `shipping-a-rag-system`.

**Light intensifiers only: "just" and "actually", almost nothing stronger.** `just` in 19 posts (median 1.3 per 1k), `actually` in 18 (1.0). The rest are rare: really 7 posts, pretty 7, very 5, extremely 1, super 1. Marketing words (powerful 4 posts, awesome 4) cluster in the earliest posts; do not imitate them.
- "**90% is Data Engineering, and the AI part is just the tip.**" (`shipping-a-rag-system`)
- "something that actually works smoothly" (`uv-the-tool`)
- Supports: `farewell-fbref`, `got-interviewed-by-ryan-day`, `i-automated-my-personal-finance`, `uv-the-tool`.

**Trade-off words: good, better, simple, fast, clean.** Used to compare options he tried, 9 to 11 posts each.
- "DeepSeek V4 Flash isn't Claude of course but for the price... the output was pretty decent." (`a-greek-god-and-two-cetaceans`)
- Supports: `from-vibes-to-metrics`, `a-greek-god-and-two-cetaceans`, `rag-is-a-data-engineering`, `shipping-a-rag-system`.

### Emphasis

**Bold marks a key term, a label, or the one main-point sentence.** Bold is in all 26 posts (median about 6 spans per post): tool names ("**uv**", "**MinIO**"), concept names ("**Golden Dataset**", "**Smart Router**"), list labels ("**Free Tier:**"), one thesis line.
- "**RAG efficiency relies on great Data Engineering.**" (`rag-is-a-data-engineering`)
- Supports: `uv-the-tool`, `from-vibes-to-metrics`, `shipping-a-rag-system`, `understanding-model-context-protocol`.

**Exclamation marks are rare.** Median 0.9 per 1k words. Question marks are mostly section-opening questions.

**No em-dashes, semicolons, ellipses or emoji in prose.** Median zero for each (agrees with `voice-mechanics.md`). Five older posts do use em-dashes (`the-art-of-football-data-scouting`, `rag-is-a-data-engineering`, `wordalisation-and-context`, `how-to-use-fbref`, `building-a-rag-system`); Ricardo confirmed the ban is his preference, so those are exceptions, not a pattern.

### Naming

**Newsletter: "The Underdoc".** It was "The NetPass" until 2026-01-12 (9 posts carry that footer); "The Underdoc" from 2026-01-30 (`from-vibes-to-metrics`) on. In prose: "this newsletter" or "my newsletter".
- "This newsletter is about building AI systems, using football analytics as the sandbox." (`embrace-your-weirdness`)
- Supports: `shipping-a-rag-system`, `wordalisation-and-context`, `how-a-football-framework`, `a-thank-you-two-ideas`.

**His own work: "I built" plus a plain noun (project, dashboard, pipeline, system), then a bold name if it has one.** "I built" 14 hits, "I created" 3, "I made" 3, "I wrote" 2, across 11 posts.
- "I built a **Smart Router**" (`shipping-a-rag-system`)
- "So I wrote a Claude Code skill called ..." (`i-automated-my-personal-finance`)
- Supports: `rag-is-a-data-engineering`, `from-vibes-to-metrics`, `a-claude-skill-to-build`, `a-greek-god-and-two-cetaceans`.

**Series posts are "article" and "series"; one-offs are "post".** "series" in 5 posts, "article" in 16; in-body links say "previous article".
- "In my previous article, I broke down how I built the **Golden Dataset**" (`from-vibes-to-metrics`)
- Supports: `building-a-rag-system`, `rag-is-a-data-engineering`, `shipping-a-rag-system`.

**The reader is "you"; the sign-off is "Till next time, Ricardo."** you/your median 15.2 per 1k (all 26 posts), "you can/you'll" in 23. "Till next time," closes 11 posts. Never "readers", "folks" or "guys".
- Supports: `embrace-your-weirdness`, `uv-the-tool`, `farewell-fbref`, `wordalisation-and-context`, `a-greek-god-and-two-cetaceans`.

**Tool and model names keep their own capitalization.** Never lowercased: LLM(s), RAG, MCP, Claude, Cursor, Python, GitHub, xG, xT, StatsBomb, Transfermarkt, Gradio, Streamlit. `uv` is always lowercase (3 posts, 28 hits). Expand acronyms on first use: "Expected Goals (xG)", "Model Context Protocol (MCP)".
- Supports: `understanding-model-context-protocol`, `building-your-own-football-analytics`, `uv-the-tool`, `building-a-rag-system`.

**FBref, spelled the site's way.** The corpus mixes `FBRef` (11), `FBref`, `FBREF` and `Fbref` (1 each, 4 posts); Ricardo chose the official "FBref" from now on.

**"football analytics": lowercase in prose, Title Case only in titles and headings.** Lowercase in running prose (17 hits); Title Case in titles (5).
- Supports: `a-thank-you-two-ideas`, `a-greek-god-and-two-cetaceans`, `using-agentic-ides`.

### Not rules (thin evidence)

Seen, but too few posts to make a rule. Do not enforce; revisit when the corpus grows.

- "HuggingFace" vs "Hugging Face": 2 posts write "HuggingFace Spaces"; the company writes "Hugging Face".
- Title Case for concepts mid-sentence ("Context Engineering", "Golden Dataset"): consistent inside 2 or 3 posts each, not a corpus habit.
- "AI engineering" / "building AI systems" as his field label: 6 posts, 4 of them in course or book titles.
- "agentic IDE(s)" and "harness" as house terms: 3 and 2 posts.
- "Wordalisation": a borrowed term (1 post), not his coinage.

### Small rules `[advisory]`
- Acronyms: expand on first use (RAG, MCP, xG), then use freely.
- Emoji: none in body text. Corpus practice.
- Bold: sparing. Corpus bolds an occasional key term or main-point statement; a post with zero bold is fine. Never general emphasis — when in doubt, don't.
- Capitalization: sentence case in prose; headings may title-case tool names only because the tools are names.

### Banned vocabulary (unless quoting or technically required)
amazing, fascinating, mind-blowing, must-read, game-changer, groundbreaking, paradigm-shifting, transformative, pivotal, paramount, outstanding, a significant leap, delve, dive into, embark, endeavour, realm, tapestry, vibrant, leverage, harness, seamlessly, seamlessly integrates, effortlessly, robust, supercharge, elevate, unlock, "unlock the real power", "the best part is", "real magic happens", "recipe for disaster", thrive, cut through the noise/hype, crucial, critical, invaluable, significant/significantly, surprisingly, simply, neatly, "Whether you're X or Y".

### Words and usage
- Flag journalese: adjectives as nouns ("greats," "notables"), chopped or padded verbs ("enthuse," "beef up"), "upcoming," "famed," "firing off" a note. It is "the death of freshness in anybody's style."
- Flag the reflex cliché chain: "waging a lonely war," "sending shock waves," "only to be met." "We are in the hands of a hack, and we know it right away. We stop reading."
- "The race in writing is not to the swift but to the original." When a flagged sentence is tired, the fix is usually a fresher word, not more words.
- Words with mismatched connotations betray carelessness: nobody "enjoys" a slump. Check that each loaded word means what the sentence needs.
- New words earn their place by filling a real need ("dropout," "launder"); jargon coinages that just sound important do not ("prioritize," "disincentive," "input/feedback" for ideas and opinions).
- Faddish tech-flavored verbs are jargon unless the domain genuinely owns them: "impact" as a verb, "grow the business," "ongoing," "leverage" as a verb.
- Note (voice-files caveat): Zinsser's grammar conservatism ("fewer/less," "that/which," "comprise") is advisory only; never apply it where it would flatten Ricardo's spoken rhythm.

## Naming consistency

Call one thing by one name for the whole piece. Do not rename the same object for variety (synonym cycling). Name tools, books and people exactly; never "an LLM" or "a book I read".
